explanation: Period family. SQL filters o.date >= '2026-03-01 00:00:00' AND o.date < '2026-06-01 00:00:00' (closed left, open right) and sums quantity_product * price with COALESCE(...,0). Matches the question and the protocol conventions; checked equivalent to the reference query.

Age on a reference date family. The question asks for customers whose completed age is exactly 25 on 2026-09-25, i.e. born from 2000-09-26 to 2001-09-25 (a one-year window). The model wrote WHERE c.birth_date = '2001-09-25': it keeps only customers born on that exact day (their 25th birthday is the reference date) and drops everyone else who is 25. The query is valid SQL and runs, but answers a different question: value 135000 instead of 590320 (too low). The reference query computes the completed age (year difference minus 1 if the birthday is not yet reached) and was checked independently.
Product list + period. SQL keeps product_id IN ('a','b','c') and the period [2026-01-01, 2026-07-01). Matches the question; checked equivalent to the reference query.
Period family, period [2026-01-01, 2026-10-01) with >= and <. Matches the question; checked equivalent to the reference query.
Period family, one-day period [2026-06-01, 2026-06-02) with >= and <. Matches the question; checked equivalent to the reference query.
Period family, period [2025-01-01, 2026-01-01). No order in 2025, so the correct answer is 0; COALESCE(SUM(...),0) returns 0 instead of NULL as the protocol requires.
Period family, period [2026-05-31, 2026-06-01): the open right bound correctly excludes orders at 2026-06-01 00:00:00. Matches the question; checked equivalent to the reference query.

Age on a reference date family. Completed age exactly 25 on 2026-09-24 means born from 2000-09-25 to 2001-09-24. The model wrote c.birth_date >= '2001-09-24' AND c.birth_date < '2001-09-25', a one-day window that keeps only customers born on 2001-09-24 (25th birthday on the reference date). Same misreading as C02: 'exactly 25' interpreted as 'turns 25 that day'. Valid SQL, wrong meaning: value 25920 instead of 605580 (too low).

Age on a reference date family. SQL uses c.birth_date BETWEEN '2000-09-27' AND '2001-09-26', which is exactly the set of customers aged 25 on 2026-09-26 (birth_date is a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' text, so BETWEEN is safe here). Correct, and checked equivalent to the reference on dense test data; shows the model's age logic is not stable across C02, C08, C09 and C11.

Age at the time of the order. SQL computes year(o.date) - year(birth_date) minus 1 if the order's month-day is before the birthday, and keeps age = 25: correct completed age at each order line. Checked equivalent to the reference query.

Age on a reference date family. Completed age exactly 25 on 2026-12-01 means born from 2000-12-02 to 2001-12-01. The model wrote c.birth_date > '2001-12-01' AND c.birth_date <= '2006-12-01': the bounds are 20 and 25 years before the date instead of 25 and 26, so it selects customers aged 20 to 24 and excludes those aged 25. Valid SQL, wrong window: value 322160 instead of 446690.
Product list over all orders: product_id IN ('a','b','c'), no date filter. Matches the question; checked equivalent to the reference query.
Product list + period: products a and c only, period [2026-04-01, 2026-05-01). Matches the question; checked equivalent to the reference query.
Product list + period [2026-10-01, 2026-12-01). No matching order, so the answer is 0; COALESCE returns 0 as required.

Period + age on a reference date. Period [2026-03-01, 2026-06-01) and birth_date between 2000-09-26 and 2001-09-25 inclusive: correct window for age 25 on 2026-09-25. Same reference date as C02, where the model failed when the age question was asked alone.

Product list + age on a reference date. Age written as birth_date <= date('2026-09-25','-25 years') AND birth_date > date('2026-09-25','-26 years'), i.e. born from 2000-09-26 to 2001-09-25: correct. Checked equivalent to the reference query.

Period + product list + age on a reference date. Period [2026-01-01, 2026-07-01), products a, b, c, birth_date in (2000-09-25, 2001-09-25]: all three filters correct. Checked equivalent to the reference query.
Period + age at the time of the order. Period [2026-05-01, 2026-06-01) and completed age at o.date = 25 (year difference minus 1 before the birthday). Checked equivalent to the reference query.
Period + product d + age on 2026-09-25 (birth_date in (2000-09-25, 2001-09-25]). All filters correct; checked equivalent to the reference query.
